A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the specificity of recombination of H and L chain is determined by a combination of the following factors: (a) the presence of the disulfide bond in the L chain, (b) the presence of a disulfide bond between the H chains, (c) the presence of free sulfhydryl groups in the L chains, and (d) differences in primary structure of the H and L chain molecules.

the specificity of the noncovalent interactions between H and L chains is related to the primary structure of these chains, which is reflected by the configuration of the chains and which determines the thermodynamic parameters of the noncovelent interactions.

the specificity of recombination between the H and the L chains is related to the specificity of the primary structure of these chains and that this specificity is expressed in the configuration of these chains.
